FOREWORD

Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 15 November 1986, after the draft finalized hy the Chemical RiIethods of Test Sectional Committee had been approved by the Textile Division Council. 0.2 Textile f?oor coverings form a large part of export of textiles. Colnur fastnrss to shampooin,q is an important parameter to check the formulation of a quality of the product for everyday USC. Hence standard method of test for detcrnrining colour fastness of textile floor covering-s to shampooing needs no emphasis.

1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard prescribes a method for determination of colour fastness of textile floor coverings, yarns and loose fibres intended for manufacture of textile floor coverings; and the tufts extracted from textile floor coverings to the action of a standard shampoo solution.
2. PRINCIPLE

of the textile floor covering, yarn, loose fibre, or tufts; in contact with specified adjacent fabrics, is immersed under pressure in a solution of shampoo buffered to PH 7'5 f 0'2. The specimen and adjacent fabrics are dried separately. The change in colnur of the specimen and the staining of the adjacent fabrics arc assessed with standard ,grey scales.
3. SAMPLING 3.1 The sample of textile Root. covering, yarn, fibrc or tufts shall be as to be representative of the lot. Sample clr-awn in so drawn accordance with the procedure laid clown in the material specification nr as agreed t.o between the buyer and ttre seller shall bc held to be rcpresenf alive of the lot.

4.6 Shampoo Solution -prepared by dissolving 1 g sodium lauryl sulphate ( active h?gradient ) and 0'2 g lauric mono-isopropanolamide in about 500 ml of deionized or distilled water. Heat, if necessary to ensure the dissolution of the surfactant. Cool to about 30�C. Prepare buffer solution by adding 14 ml of 0.5 M citric acid to 372 ml of 0'5 M disodium hydrogen phosphate ( see also IS : 3225-1965* ). Add the buffer solution to the surfactant solution. Check the PH to 7'5 & 0.2. Finally make the total volume of shampoo solution up to one litrc. 4.7 Adjacent Fabrics

4.7.1 When the specimen is in the form of a textile floor covering, two adjacent fabrics 50 mm X 40 mm are required, one piece made of the same fibre as that in the specimen or that predominating in the case of blends, the second piece made of any other fibre ( see Table 1 ). If the staining of additional fibres is of interest, two or more specimens shall be tested separately. 4.7.2 When the specimen is in the form of yarn or loose fibre, two adjacent fabrics 100 mm x 40 mm are required, one piece made of the same fibre as that in the specimen or that predominating in the case of blends, the second piece made of any other fibre ( see Table 1 ). If the staining of additional fibrcs is of interest, two or more specimens shall be tested separately. 4.7.3 When the specimen is in the form of tufts extracted from a textile floor covering, two adjacent fabrics 50 mm x 40 mm are required, one piece made of cotton, to act solely as a support for the tufts, the second piece made of the same fibre as that in the specimen *Method for preparation of buffer solutions.

floor covering is to be tested, cut a specimen 100 mm X from which any integral foam underlay has been removed, and cover the use surface with the two pieces of adjacent fabrics 50 mm X 40 mm ( see 4.7.1 ). `Method tMethod for evaluating change in colour (first rcuision). for evaluating staining (JFrst retision ).

KS : 11969- 1986 , 5.2 If yarn is to be tested,

sew a uniform layer of parallel 100 mm lengths, weighing 0'4 g, to one edge of one of the piece of adjacent fabrics 100 mm x 40 mm (see 4.7.2) Cover with the other piece 100 mm X 40 mm and sew along the same edge to form a composite specimen.

5.3 If loose fibre is to be tested, comb and compress 0'4 g of the fibre Place this between the two into a uniform layer 100 mm X 40 mm. pieces of adjacent fabrics 100 mm x 40 mm (see 4.7.2 ) and sew along two opposite sides to form a composite specimen. 5.4 If tufts extracted from textile floor coverings are to be tested, sew a number of identical tufts weighing approximately 012 g on to a piece of cotton adjacent fabric 50 mm x 40 mm. Cover with a piece of adjacent fabric 50 mm x 40 mm (see 4.7.3) and sew along one side to form a composite specimen. 6. PROCEDURE the composite specimen in the flat-bottomed dish (see 4.2 ) and pour over the specimen a quantity of the shampoo solution (see 4.6) at 27 f 2�C sufficient to give a liquor ratio of 50 : 1 Ensure that the specimen is thoroughly wetted by the solution and lies flat. Cover with the glass plate ( see 4.3), press with the fingers to remove air bubbles, and place the weight-piece (see 4.4) on top of the glass plate. A composite specimen of tufts should be placed in the dish with the cotton on the underside.
Nom - Care should be taken with the solution during testing. so that the material of thl, weight does not react

6.1 Place

6.2 Allow it to stand at 27 f 2'C for 15 minutes in the perspirometer. Remove the weight-piece and pour off the shampoo solution without removing the glass plate, replace the weight-piece and allow it to stand, for a further period of three hours at 27 f 2 C. Separate the specimen 6.3 Remove the weight-piece and glass plate. from the adjacent fabrics and allow the specimen and the adjacent fabrics to dry apart in air at a temperature not exceeding 60�C. 6.4 Assess the change in colour of the specimen and the staining of the adjacent fabrics with the grey scales (see IS : 768-1982* and IS : 769-1982t). When tufts are being tested, the staining of the cotton support need not be assessed. *Method TMethod for e raluating for vvaluating change staining in colour (jirst revision ). (jirst revidon ).
